header: My rule (step 45b): a question that names a large department (CO & CC, main hospital, L & D ...) must be answered for ALL its rows. The model is told the ids (context.ts departmentFamilies), but a model can ignore a hint, and a confident wrong answer is worse than none. Live, 24 Oct 2026: "main hospital" -> LIKE '%hospital%' found 2 of the 6 medical rows and counted 0 executives "hydraulic lab" -> LIKE '%hydraulic lab%' found no row and counted 0 "l&d" -> LIKE '%l d%' also matches the text "contro[l d]eptt": it counted ENVIRONMENT CONTROL DEPTT and called it L&D So I work out WHICH ROWS the model's SQL selects (by id, by code, or by a LIKE or = on the name, read against the live department list), and if they are not the family, I send the model back with the exact ids. I look at the RESULT, not the form: LIKE '%co and cc%' passes (it selects exactly the CO & CC rows), code IN (92500, 92530) passes, department_id IN (...) passes. A named SECTION is respected: when the question carries a word that only the selected rows have ("sms ccp", "hospital office"), a part of the family is accepted. Like the other soft rules of the pipeline it is used on the first two attempts only: I never fail a question over it. Step 48a: when the mistake can be mended with certainty, I mend the SQL instead (repairFamilies), at once and with no second model call: live, 24 Oct 2026 17:41, the model wrote code IN (135,180,161,126,89,1), the row IDS as department CODES, three times in a row, the check sent it back twice and the third attempt (never checked) showed 0 -- after 80 seconds, because every extra model call spends about 6,000 tokens and Groq's per-minute limit made the next one wait 23 and 45 seconds.

symbols.name: STOP
doc: Little words that are in many department names and in many questions: they never tell which SECTION a question means, so I ignore them.

symbols.name: codeNumbers
doc: Returns the numbers an SQL puts after "code IN (...)" or "code = ..." (department_code too).

symbols.name: rowsSelectedBy
symbols.sig: export function rowsSelectedBy(sql: string, departments: DepartmentRow[]): DepartmentRow[]
doc: Returns the rows of the live list that an SQL selects through its department conditions (none when it has no department condition I can read).

symbols.name: genericWords
doc: Returns the words that name the family itself (its nicknames, or its own name). A row word NOT in here tells which section a row is ("ccp" is not a nickname of SMS, it is a section of it).

symbols.name: checkFamilies
symbols.sig: export function checkFamilies(question: string, sql: string, departments: DepartmentRow[]): string | null
doc: Returns a sentence for the model when its SQL does not cover a department family the question names; null when it does (or when the question names none).

symbols.name: repairFamilies
symbols.sig: export function repairFamilies(question: string, sql: string, departments: DepartmentRow[]): string | null
doc: Mends the SQL when it covers the department family a question names wrongly (ids written as codes, a LIKE on the name that finds other rows or none, one row of several ...): the first department_id IN (...) / department_code IN (...) -- a list or a sub-query, found by matching the brackets -- becomes department_id IN (the family's ids). Returns the mended SQL, or null when nothing needs mending or the mistake is not one I can mend with certainty:
- the question names two or more families (a comparison): the model's own grouping would be lost, so I send it back instead;
- the SQL has no department_id IN / department_code IN to put the ids into;
- the mended SQL would not pass checkFamilies again.

symbols.name: withDepartmentIds
symbols.sig: export function withDepartmentIds(sql: string, ids: number[]): string | null
doc: Returns the SQL with its first department_id / department_code IN (...) -- a list or a sub-query, found by matching the brackets -- replaced by department_id IN (the ids); null when the SQL has no such list (or its brackets do not close). Shared by repairFamilies (step 48a) and repairNamedRows (step 49b, namedRows.ts).
